quiz.0.question: In which decade did the Barolo Boys revolution begin?
quiz.0.explanation: The Barolo Boys movement emerged in the 1980s — led by Elio Altare, Enrico Scavino and others — who adopted small French barriques, shorter maceration and radical new techniques that split the Barolo world into 'traditionalists' vs 'modernists'.
quiz.1.question: What type of oak barrel do traditional-style Barolo producers principally use?
quiz.1.options.1: Large Slavonian or Italian oak casks (botti grandi, 25–50 hl+)
quiz.1.explanation: Traditionalists use large Slavonian (or Italian) oak botti (2,500–5,000+ litres), ageing the wine for 3–5+ years — imparting minimal oak flavour while slowly refining the tannins.
quiz.2.question: Giacomo Conterno's Monfortino grapes come from which MGA?
quiz.2.explanation: Monfortino Riserva — Giacomo Conterno's greatest wine — comes exclusively from the Francia vineyard in Serralunga d'Alba, owned by the Conterno family.
quiz.3.question: In blind tasting, how can you quickly distinguish traditional from modern Barolo?
quiz.3.options.0: Modern Barolo always has higher alcohol
quiz.3.options.1: Traditional Barolo: pale, orange-edged colour + tar & roses + austere tannins; Modern: deeper colour + vanilla + rounder, softer tannins
quiz.3.options.2: Traditional Barolo smells of oak; Modern smells of fruit
quiz.3.options.3: There is no reliable way to distinguish them blind
quiz.3.explanation: Traditional Barolo: pale garnet with orange rim, classic tar-roses-dried violet aromas, strict chalky tannins, high acidity, long evolution. Modern Barolo: deeper ruby, vanilla-fruit bouquet, rounder tannins, more immediately approachable.
